lesson.subject: general-knowledge
lesson.title: Life in Tanzania
lesson.summary: Explore daily life in Arusha, Tanzania, and compare it with life near you.
learning_objectives: Compare similarities and differences with home

standards.text: Understand geographical similarities and differences through studying the human and physical geography of a small area in a contrasting non-European country

success_criteria: I can find Tanzania on a map
I can name physical and human features
I can say what is the same and different
lesson.real_life: Swahili and Urdu greetings, the Muslim heritage of Zanzibar, and community ties between Britain, Pakistan and East Africa.

warm_up.prompt: What do we call very big land with many countries?

blocks.markdown: Today's big question: what is life like in Tanzania?
blocks.say: Today we visit Tanzania, a country in Africa. We will meet a city called Arusha.

blocks.alt: A giraffe walking across dry golden grassland at sunset between acacia trees
blocks.caption: A giraffe on the African savannah at sunset.
blocks.credit: Photo by Wouter Groote Veldman on Unsplash
blocks.say: A giraffe walks across the savannah at sunset. Wild animals live in Tanzania.

blocks.markdown: Africa is a **continent**, not a country.
blocks.say: Africa is a huge continent. It has fifty-four countries. Tanzania is one of them.

scenes.caption: Africa.
scenes.say: Find Africa on the map. It is south of Europe.

scenes.caption: Tanzania.
scenes.say: Tanzania is in East Africa, next to the Indian Ocean.

scenes.say: Tanzania's neighbours include Kenya and Uganda.

question.explanation: Africa is a continent with many countries.

blocks.alt: A rocky mountain top with patches of ice and snow above a layer of cloud under a deep blue sky
blocks.caption: A high mountain top with ice and snow above the clouds. Kilimanjaro is a mountain like this.
blocks.credit: Photo by Harshil Gudka on Unsplash
blocks.say: Mount Kilimanjaro is the highest mountain in Africa. It stands in Tanzania.

blocks.markdown: A **physical feature** is made by nature.
blocks.say: It is so tall that it has snow on top, even near the Equator.

scenes.caption: Tall.
scenes.say: Kilimanjaro is a very tall mountain.

scenes.caption: Snow.
scenes.say: The top is cold and snowy.

scenes.caption: Visitors.
scenes.say: People travel from all over to see it.

question.explanation: Tanzania is a country in Africa.

blocks.title: Layla's pen pal in Arusha
blocks.transcript: Layla gets a letter from a pen pal in Arusha. Arusha is in Tanzania, in Africa. The photo shows a busy market. There are mangoes, bananas and tomatoes. Layla's market in Lahore has fruit too. But Arusha has Mount Meru and Kilimanjaro nearby. Layla writes back. She says Jambo and Asante. Places can be alike and different. Friends can be too.
blocks.caption: Layla receives a photo from an Arusha pen pal and compares the market with her own.

blocks.say: Let us remember. Africa is a continent. Tanzania is a country with a tall mountain.

scenes.say: In Arusha, many people speak Swahili. In Lahore, many speak Urdu and Punjabi.

blocks.markdown: A **pen pal** is a friend who writes to you.
blocks.say: A pen pal is a friend you write to. Let us write to a child in Arusha.

scenes.caption: Hello.
scenes.say: Start with a greeting. Say Jambo, which means hello in Swahili.

scenes.caption: My place.
scenes.say: Tell them about your street. Say what you can see and hear.

scenes.caption: Thank you.
scenes.say: End with a kind word. Say Asante, which means thank you.

blocks.markdown: Ask questions with respect and curiosity.
blocks.say: Ask kind questions about their place. What is your school like? What do you eat?

scenes.caption: A question.
scenes.say: Ask about their day. What do you do after school?

scenes.caption: Food.
scenes.say: Ask about their food. What is your favourite meal?

scenes.caption: Listen.
scenes.say: Listen to the answer. Say what is the same as yours.
